We've seen a lot of discussion about the new Quick Menu layout, and we get it: when familiar buttons move, muscle memory takes the hit.

This layout change is part of a broader shift to bring Events and Groups closer to the center of the VRChat experience. Surfacing what's happening live helps more players discover and join experiences together, which is a big focus for us right now.

Right now, this layout is part of an ongoing experiment. We're testing how changes like this affect how people navigate and discover social experiences in VRChat. We need to see how it performs at scale once it's live before deciding what sticks and what needs another pass.

Feedback is a key part of that process, as is data, A/B testing, etc. What you share here helps us spot friction that metrics alone can't capture. We'll be watching feedback closely after launch as well, and the results of both player sentiment and data will guide what comes next.

btw: the old "expando" button (which some folks have mentioned) and the new "Live Now" button both open the same place. They go to the main menu's hub for events and worlds (which used to be launchpad, and is now Live Now). That's why we removed the little expando guy, it's duplicate behavior
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name} Hi Tupper, are there perhaps considerations to rename "Live Now" to something more recognisable?
@{62770b2ab9aa4552a0459dc1|full_name}: If you have suggestions or feedback, please feel free to make a new post! This post is about the quick menu UI.

I understand that the Launch Pad's expand button became redundant, but I will say personally its removal was the most jarring QM change for me, given how often I typically pressed it. It also seems like a bad move in terms of consistency, since every other QM tab has an expand button in that exact spot.

It has been essentially *replaced* with the report button.
they could also improve the menu by not having a giant advertising billboard take up half of the launchpad

details:
The new QM Launchpad layout currently requires users to retrain their muscle memory and feels somewhat clunky to use.

I would like to suggest considering a design that more closely resembles the 4x2 grid button layout, as this could help maintain existing user familiarity and improve overall accessibility to features.

Please consider changing the design.

Note that the attached image is one I made.
